To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the reaction of aromatic diacids and trimesic with APTES at 220 °c results in the formation of ladder-like polysilsiesquioxanes.
the reaction of PA and TA with APTES at 220 ° C yields a ladder-like polysiloxane and a cyclic polyimides, respectively.
the reaction of phthalic acid with APTES results in the formation of an aromatic imide-functionalized polyorganosilsesquioxanes with improved thermal properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation and characterization of a new type of organic-inorganic nanohybrid materials.
the preparation and characterization of a series of organic-inorganic nanomaterials based on the condensation reaction of phthalic and trimesic acids with APTES.
the preparation of a novel organic-inorganic hybrid material via the sol-gel route and its thermal and structural properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reaction of PA with aminopropyltri-ethoxysilanes (APTES) results in a cyclic polyimido-silsesquioxanes (CPI-SQs).
the thermal imidisation of poly(amic acid)s derived from APTES, PA, and TA at 220 °c results in the formation of a ladder-like polysilsequioxane with a cyclic polyimides moiety.

the thermal imidizaton at 220 ° C of PA with APTS (1:1 and PA with APTS 1:2) yields ladder-like polyimide-POSS materials, whereas TA with APTS (molar ratios of 1:1 or 1:2), imidized at 220 °c, results in a crosslinked network structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a new aromatic polyimide functionalized with polysilsesquoxanes can be prepared via the sol-gel route.
we have succeeded in the preparation of an organic-inorganic nanohybrid with an aromatic imide moiety via a sol-gel route.
the organic-inorganics hybrid materials are promising candidates for the development of new functional materials.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the reaction of APTES with PA and TA at elevated temperature leads to the formation of novel organic-inorganic hybrid materials, whose thermal stability can be tuned by the molar ratio of the organic acids to the silane precursor and the reaction temperature.
a new aromatic imide-containing organic-inorganic hybrid material has been prepared and characterized.
the sol-gel route is a promising approach for the preparation of novel organic-inorganic hybrid materials.
